subject.title: The Skill Accumulation Problem: How many skills before your agent gets confused?

question: Should ClawHub own a skill-accumulation governance surface, and if so should the first scoped slice be task-context recommendations, conflict/dependency metadata, load-policy guidance, or docs-only best practices?
rationale: The remaining work is not a broken implementation path; it defines new registry/runtime semantics that could affect publisher contracts, local privacy, and OpenClaw load behavior.

options.title: Define a narrow metadata RFC first
options.body: Capture a minimal contract for conflicts, dependencies, load policy, privacy, and pinning before implementation, then split schema/API/UI/CLI work into follow-up issues.

options.title: Ship docs-only guidance now
options.body: Document best practices for pruning, layering, and pinning skills while deferring registry/runtime behavior until there is more user evidence.

options.title: Defer to OpenClaw runtime or plugins
options.body: Keep ClawHub focused on catalog metadata and leave active skill selection or collision resolution to runtime/plugin surfaces.

recommendation.title: Define a narrow metadata RFC first
recommendation.body: Capture a minimal contract for conflicts, dependencies, load policy, privacy, and pinning before implementation, then split schema/API/UI/CLI work into follow-up issues.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is CODEOWNERS-listed for the central backend/API/schema/CLI surfaces this product contract would touch.
